## Fast Once Is Not the Same as Robustly Fast {#sec-lay-ch23}

## A Concrete Picture

A racing setup that wins one qualifying lap may lose its advantage in wind,
tire wear, or traffic. Comparing setups therefore requires a task and a declared
range of conditions. A probability distribution helps when the question concerns
how often an outcome occurs; a worst-case comparison can instead use a specified
set of disturbances without assigning probabilities.

The same distinction matters in a swing model. A command that gives high nominal
club speed may become sensitive to timing, initial state, shaft properties, or
the permitted face error. Robustness asks which conclusions survive specified
changes. It does not mean immunity to every disturbance, and a repeatable slow
swing is not automatically a useful one.

![Two Projections of the Same Eight Programs on Six Held-Out Cases.](figures/proximal_distal_companion/fig_companion_tradeoff_map.svg){#fig-lay-tradeoff width=100% fig-alt="Eight numbered programs from the coupled uncertainty study appear in both panels. The left compares mean planar face–path error with tenth-percentile delivery speed. The right compares ninetieth-percentile peak individual hand force with delivery-speed standard deviation. Colors identify programs, not load; no frontier or continuous interpolation is drawn."}

The points in @fig-lay-tradeoff are recomputed from the archived outputs discussed
below. They are two projections of a five-objective comparison. A point that
looks inferior in one panel can remain nondominated when another objective is
included. Lines between programs would not establish that intermediate commands
achieve intermediate outcomes.

## How the Mechanism Works

### State the Question Before Choosing a Score

Let a policy $\pi$ specify a command program or a feedback rule, and let $\theta$
describe uncertain parameters, initial state, and disturbances. Their modeled
outcome can be written $Y(\pi,\theta)$. Name the endpoint as carefully as the
policy: speed at a fixed time, speed at a specified crossing, and ball-impact
delivery answer different questions. If the event never occurs, the outcome
needs an explicit missing-event or failure rule.

A useful comparison fixes the model, admissible policy family, actuator limits,
initial-state convention, and endpoint. It then states what varies and what
counts as acceptable. The policy itself may react to measurements, but the
feedback rule and available information must be fixed before evaluation.
Allowing one program perfect knowledge of a future impact time changes its
information advantage, not just its mechanics.

Mean speed, lower-tail speed, accuracy, load, and energy are different
objectives. A weighted score requires units or normalization and explicit
weights. Changing metres per second to another unit must not silently change
the selected policy. A force minimum also does not imply minimum joint torque
or muscle effort; those relationships require the relevant mechanical and
physiological model.

### The Tail Depends on Whether Larger Is Better

For speed treated as a reward, a low percentile summarizes poor-speed cases.
For a nonnegative face error treated as a loss, large values are adverse, so an
upper percentile describes the difficult cases. Reducing *lower-tail error*
could merely improve the already accurate swings while leaving large misses
unchanged. A hypothetical speed/error trade must identify the adverse tail
and must not be presented as a measured result.

For a scalar outcome $Z$, define its population quantile at level $0<\alpha<1$ by

$$
q_\alpha(Z)=\inf\{z:\Pr(Z\leq z)\geq\alpha\}.
$$

A quantile is a threshold, not the average severity beyond it. An empirical
quantile also needs an interpolation convention. With six speed observations, the
linear 10th-percentile estimator used in the provider code is halfway between
the smallest and second-smallest values. It is not six observations of a
10-percent tail, nor a demonstrated guarantee for 90 percent of future golfers.

Use the same sampled cases for paired policy comparisons where the experiment
allows it. This reveals whether one policy helps the same difficult cases.
The difference between two policy quantiles generally differs from the quantile
of their paired differences. In the archived early-restrain/late-drive comparison,
the former is about 0.289 m/s and the latter about 0.271 m/s. Neither says that
every case improves by that amount.

### Severity, Probability, and Worst Case Are Different

For an integrable loss $L$ calculated from the modeled outcomes, conditional
value at risk can be defined by the
Rockafellar–Uryasev formula [@rockafellar2002]:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(L)
&=\min_{\eta\in\mathbb R}F_\alpha(\eta),\\
F_\alpha(\eta)&=\eta+\frac{\mathbb E[(L-\eta)_+]}{1-\alpha},\\
(z)_+&=\max(z,0).
\end{aligned}
$$

It measures the average of the worst $1-\alpha$ fraction of loss probability.
At a probability atom, use the appropriate fraction of mass at the threshold;
simply averaging observations strictly above the quantile can give another
quantity. For four equally weighted losses $0,0,0,10$, the 50-percent CVaR is
$5$, whereas the mean strictly above the median is $10$. This example explains
the definition, not a golf measurement.

A chance constraint asks for a probability of acceptable outcomes. If all
delivery conditions matter together, write a joint condition, such as

$$
\Pr(E\leq e_{\max},\ F\leq f_{\max})\geq1-\varepsilon,
$$

where $E$ is declared delivery error, $F$ is a declared force metric, and the
thresholds and distribution are specified. Two separate 90-percent success
rates need not give 90-percent joint success: disjoint 10-percent failure sets
leave only 80 percent satisfying both. A chosen hand-force threshold is a
model constraint, not an established injury threshold.

A set-based worst-case objective instead examines $\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
L(\pi,\theta)$ over a declared uncertainty set $\Theta$. The largest loss among
a finite set of sampled cases is generally only a lower bound on that supremum.
Dense sampling, local derivatives, and a successful optimizer do not alone
certify the unsampled set. Conversely, an implausible range edge can make a
worst-case design unnecessarily conservative. Quantiles, CVaR, probability
constraints, and worst-case bounds answer different questions; none is the
automatic definition of a good swing.

### What the Registered Coupled Study Actually Compares

The provider study uses a planar moving-base model with two articulated arms,
two solved hand reactions, and one flexible shaft mode. It varies 12 engineering
inputs spanning geometry, inertias, base stiffness, damping, grip separation,
shaft properties, command delay, lag, and an impedance coefficient. A
deterministic Latin-hypercube design supplies 24 global screening cases, six
training cases, and six independently generated held-out cases. The seeds are
8426, 8449, and 8450, respectively. Every candidate uses the same cases within
a split.

These ranges are not fitted golfer-population distributions. The implementation
permutes strata and jitters within the middle portion of each stratum; it is
a declared space-filling design, not a collection of independent identically
distributed human trials. Delivery is evaluated at 0.24 s with a 4 ms integration
step, not at a ball collision. Small constraint and contact-power residuals
check particular numerical identities; they do not by themselves bound
trajectory integration error or establish convergence of tail estimates.

Eight programs were preselected: passive wrist, early drive, late drive,
restrain then drive, higher impedance, later release, lower drive, and early
restrain. Their names identify parameter choices, not eight observed human
techniques. In particular, early restrain blends its right-wrist command from
$-2$ to $+4$ N m beginning at 0.10 s, while late drive blends from $0$ to
$+5$ N m beginning at 0.14 s. The command transition lasts 35 ms; the paired
left-wrist target is $-0.65$ times the right-wrist target in the model's signed
coordinates. These signs do not alone identify a net club couple or an
anatomical muscle action.

The actuator applies pure delay, a discretized first-order command lag with a
rate-limited state increment, velocity-dependent resistance, and asymmetric
torque–velocity clipping. Its so-called impedance term is proportional to
actuator velocity in this implementation; it is not a measured muscle stiffness
or a full reflex model. Thus the command schedules are preselected, while
delivered torque also depends on velocity. The rate limit on the lag state
does not by itself bound every change after velocity-dependent clipping.
Even the program named passive wrist can retain modeled velocity resistance.

The five objectives are:

1. Maximize 10th-percentile delivery speed.
2. Minimize mean absolute planar face–path error.
3. Minimize the 90th percentile of peak individual-hand force.
4. Minimize mean integrated squared delivered joint torque.
5. Minimize the sample standard deviation of delivery speed.

The face–path proxy is the absolute wrapped difference between the modeled
planar face direction and terminal velocity direction. It is not three-dimensional
clubface delivery or ball dispersion. The force statistic first takes the
largest force norm over both hands and all recorded times in each rollout,
then takes a percentile across cases. The squared-torque integral has units
$\mathrm{N^2\,m^2\,s}$; it is not mechanical work, metabolic energy, or measured
muscular effort. Standard deviation measures spread, not tracking stability,
recovery from disturbance, or probability of meeting a target.

### What the Archived Results Establish

Independent recomputation from the stored arrays gives seven nondominated
programs on the training cases and eight on the held-out cases. Early restrain
has held-out 10th-percentile speed of approximately 4.706 m/s versus 4.417 m/s
for late drive. Its mean planar error is approximately $5.44^\circ$,
compared with $1.58^\circ$ for late drive. This is a speed/error tradeoff for two specified
schedules in six cases. It does not isolate the early opposing interval:
the compared schedules also have different onset and late-command values.

The implementation selects programs using **training** objectives. Its
balanced, equal-range Chebyshev rule chooses later release, the speed-priority rule
chooses early restrain, and the load-priority rule chooses higher impedance.
The balanced rule minimizes the largest objective disadvantage after scaling
each objective by its range across the training candidates. Those data-dependent
scales encode a choice and can change when candidates change. The held-out
outputs evaluate the selected programs and other candidates; they are not the
data used by those selection rules.

Omitting one held-out case at a time changes Pareto membership. Passive wrist,
early drive, late drive, and higher impedance remain nondominated in all six
omissions; restrain then drive, lower drive, and early restrain do so in five;
later release does so in four. This is a perturbation check on six cases, not
a confidence interval for a population frontier. The complete recomputation
and original arrays are linked in the review evidence.

### A Pareto Set Is Relative to Its Feasible Comparisons

A feasible policy is dominated if another feasible policy is no worse on every
declared objective and strictly better on at least one. Nondominated policies
form the Pareto set; their objective vectors form the corresponding front.
Restricting the comparison to eight candidates gives a *candidate* Pareto set.
Another admissible policy not evaluated here might improve every objective.

For example, the loss vectors $(0,2)$, $(2,0)$, and $(1,1)$ are mutually
nondominated. An untested feasible vector $(-1,-1)$ would dominate all three.
The archived study therefore leaves a universal optimum unsupported; it does
not prove that none exists over every admissible control program. Likewise,
nondominance in five sample summaries is neither stochastic dominance nor
superiority in every individual case.

A tradeoff plot makes the decision visible but does not assign its values.
Speed, accuracy, force exposure, and repeatability can be weighted, constrained,
or considered separately. Normalization and weights must be chosen and reported.
A weighted sum can miss parts of a nonconvex front, and a continuous line drawn
between discrete policies is not evidence of realizable intermediate performance.

### Construct Uncertainty Without Hiding the Experiment

Separate execution variability, participant variation, uncertain calibration,
unknown physical parameters, and model discrepancy where possible. Declare
ranges, distributions, dependence, temporal structure, and their evidence.
Independent draws of geometrically related parameters can create impossible
bodies or grips; constraint-consistent initial states and admissibility checks
belong inside the design. Merely increasing the number of simulations does not
repair an omitted mechanism or an unjustified distribution.

Timing, amplitude, direction, and allocation perturbations can expose different
weaknesses. Choose temporal correlations and smoothness to match the mechanism
under investigation; white or independent noise is not automatically wrong,
but a numerical sampling convention is not an execution model. A local
derivative describes a neighborhood and can miss distant failures, contact-mode
changes, or a missing event. Broad timing plateaus are useful only relative to
a performance tolerance, the other disturbances, and the resolution of the
search.

Paired simulations should share exogenous cases while retaining the state
changes caused by each policy. Resetting transmission state to make two trials
look matched changes the intervention. Chapter 3 explains that distinction;
Chapter 14 explains finite preparation and role reversal. A comparison of
policy families should declare their admissible controls, resource constraints,
tuning procedure, and computational budget. Equal budgets reduce one
confound but do not prove equal optimization quality or equal physiological
feasibility.

### Preserve Failures and the Denominator

Record how many cases were attempted, solved, physically admissible, and
evaluated at the required endpoint. A numerical failure, an impossible contact,
a missing impact event, and a valid but poor delivery are different outcomes.
Investigate numerical failures with refinement or an independent method;
do not silently delete them or automatically relabel them as physical failures.

A distribution conditional on successful solves must carry that condition.
If a case's loss is unknown, report missingness and bounds or an explicit
penalty rule rather than inventing its value. Discarding the worst observed
case can improve a reported tail without improving any policy. A failure rate
among completed trials also has a different denominator from a failure rate
among all attempted trials. Publish both the accounting and the metric rules.

### Keep Selection Separate From Evaluation

Use development cases to explore policies, validation cases for tuning choices,
and an untouched evaluation set for the final claim. The eight-program archive
contains training and held-out splits, not a separate three-way validation
exercise. It demonstrates a bounded comparison, not a completed robust-control
optimization pipeline. Repeatedly modifying the program after viewing held-out
results consumes that independence.

Choose splits for the deployment question. Unseen-person prediction requires
participant separation; personalization for a known golfer requires evaluation
on genuinely new sessions or conditions and separation from that person's
calibration data. Randomly mixing correlated swings between training and test
sets can exaggerate transfer. Calibration also has scope: nominal 80-percent
coverage should be assessed across enough relevant unseen cases, with sampling
uncertainty and subgroup checks. Good average coverage can conceal poor coverage
for one participant or regime.

Personalization does not require every parameter to be uniquely identifiable
if the target prediction is stable across all plausible parameter sets.
Conversely, a precise parameter estimate under the wrong model is not reliable
prediction. Show the uncertainty that changes the decision, and withhold
confident technique prescriptions when predictive qualification is missing.

### Compare Model Tiers and Human Evidence Explicitly

Parameter sensitivity, numerical convergence, structural model changes, and
transfer to people are separate tests. A planar fixed-base ranking may change
when base motion, shaft memory, spatial contact, or delay is introduced.
Define how policies, observations, initial states, and constraints correspond
between tiers. A ranking reversal identifies a dependency to investigate;
it does not automatically identify the added physical mechanism as its cause.

Likewise, a negative torque component must name an axis, frame, and time window.
Persistence of its sign is different from persistence of a performance benefit.
A bimodal outcome distribution can arise from nonlinear transformations or
sampling choices as well as subgroups or competing mechanisms. A histogram
alone cannot decide among those explanations.

Glazier's discussion of movement variability and McPhee's review of golf models
provide methodological context [@glazier2011; @mcphee2022]. They are not validation
of the eight-program ranking or a certificate of individual robustness.
Measured responses to appropriately designed perturbations would test specified
predictions, including timing, recovery, and uncertainty. Human adaptation absent
from the model can require narrowing the claim or changing the controller model;
it cannot be inferred from the synthetic ensemble.

### Reader Lab: Make the Robustness Claim Auditable

Start with two policies, a common set of admissible cases, and fixed outcome
definitions. Plot their individual results as well as means, adverse tails, and
paired differences. State whether uncertainty is sampled probabilistically or
bounded as a set. Keep the original sample counts, unsuccessful cases, and the
quantile convention alongside the figure.

Then vary one declared assumption: the error tolerance, a parameter dependence,
the sampling design, or the model tier. Recompute the comparison without
retuning on the evaluation set. Add a simple baseline and report where the
ordering reverses. A ranking that survives these tests is evidence within their
scope, not proof against every future change.

An open modeling tool should preserve these qualifications in exported tables
and figures. It can flag violations of known input bounds but cannot guarantee
detection of unknown model inadequacy. Separate an exploratory prediction from
a qualified recommendation. A useful report identifies which measurement or
experiment would most reduce the uncertainty affecting the choice.

## Where the Picture Breaks

The racing analogy motivates a comparison across conditions; it does not imply
that a golf downswing has the same feedback opportunities as a lap. A constructed
ensemble also differs from repeated measurements of people. Denser sampling of
known variables cannot make an omitted disturbance disappear.

**Model Result:** The archived eight-program comparison reproduces a conditional
speed/error tradeoff and sample-dependent nondominance. It supports no universally
best policy and does not exclude better untested policies.

**Measurement Boundary:** The endpoint, force statistic, and effort metric are
declared model quantities. Participant-held-out measurements, appropriate outcome
definitions, and calibrated predictive uncertainty are still needed for human
robustness claims.

**Hypothesis:** Preload or an opposing command interval may improve selected
outcomes under some delays and uncertainties. Isolating that mechanism requires
matched comparisons beyond two schedules that differ in several parameters.

**Practical Interpretation:** Ask how often the intended delivery succeeds,
under which changes, with which error and load consequences, and how much of
that answer comes from measurements rather than modeling assumptions.
